key_insight: Predictive triboelectric nanogenerator design requires linking evolving real contact area and contact-dependent charge generation and decay to electrical output across length scales.
engineering_relevance: Connecting material properties, interface mechanics and circuit response can guide reliable low-frequency energy harvesters and self-powered sensors.
method: Review polymeric, inorganic, composite and natural materials for charge behavior, compliance and durability.
Assess models from molecular calculations and rough-contact mechanics to device electrostatics and equivalent circuits.
Organize applications by device scale and propose staged validation of mechanics, electrostatics and circuit response.
evidence_signal: The review assesses model inputs, predictions and experimental validation evidence; the abstract reports no quantitative performance benchmarks.
watch_item: Prescribed surface charge, idealized geometries and nominal contact-area assumptions can limit predictions under realistic loading.
paper_title: Triboelectric nanogenerators across length scales: linking materials, multiscale modelling and applications
